textbookText: 121. According to the kinetic theory of gases, gas molecules are considered to be: A) Point masses in continuous, random motion, with negligible volume compared to the container B) Fixed in position with no motion C) Arranged in an ordered lattice like a solid D) Attracted strongly to each other at all times

122. The kinetic theory assumes that collisions between gas molecules (and with container walls) are: A) Perfectly elastic, with no net loss of kinetic energy B) Perfectly inelastic, losing all kinetic energy C) Non-existent, since molecules never collide D) Only elastic at very high temperatures

123. According to kinetic theory, the pressure exerted by a gas is due to: A) Continuous collisions of gas molecules with the walls of the container B) The weight of the gas molecules pressing down C) Chemical bonding between gas molecules and the container D) The gas molecules sticking to the container walls

124. The average kinetic energy of gas molecules is directly proportional to: A) The absolute temperature of the gas B) The pressure of the gas alone C) The volume of the container alone D) The molar mass of the gas

125. According to kinetic theory, at the same temperature, all gases have: A) The same average kinetic energy per molecule, regardless of their identity or molar mass B) The same root-mean-square (rms) speed, regardless of molar mass C) The same volume regardless of pressure D) The same density, regardless of molar mass
126. The root-mean-square (rms) speed of gas molecules is given by: A) √(3RT/M), where M is molar mass B) 3RT/M C) √(RT/3M) D) RT/M²

127. A lighter gas molecule (lower molar mass), at the same temperature as a heavier gas, will have: A) A higher rms speed than the heavier gas (since KE is the same but mass differs) B) A lower rms speed than the heavier gas C) Exactly the same rms speed as the heavier gas D) Zero rms speed

128. Kinetic theory explains Boyle's law (PV = constant at fixed T) by noting that decreasing volume: A) Increases the frequency of molecular collisions with the walls, increasing pressure B) Decreases the average kinetic energy of the molecules C) Has no effect on collision frequency D) Decreases the number of molecules present

129. Which of the following is an assumption of the kinetic theory regarding intermolecular forces in an ideal gas? A) Intermolecular forces of attraction/repulsion are negligible except during collision B) Intermolecular forces are extremely strong and dominate molecular behavior C) Molecules are held in a fixed lattice by strong forces D) Intermolecular forces increase indefinitely with distance

130. According to kinetic theory, increasing the temperature of a gas at constant volume increases pressure because: A) Molecules move faster (higher KE) and collide with walls more frequently and forcefully B) The number of molecules increases C) The molecules become larger in size D) The container walls become more permeable

131. Maxwell–Boltzmann distribution describes: A) The distribution of molecular speeds among gas molecules at a given temperature, showing a range rather than a single fixed speed B) The exact single speed of every molecule in a gas C) The distribution of molecular colors in a gas D) The distribution of pressure only, not speed

132. As temperature increases, the Maxwell-Boltzmann speed distribution curve for a gas: A) Shifts toward higher speeds and becomes broader/flatter B) Shifts toward lower speeds and becomes narrower C) Remains completely unchanged D) Becomes a single vertical line at one exact speed

133. The kinetic theory of gases provides a microscopic (molecular) explanation for: A) The macroscopic gas laws (Boyle's, Charles's, Gay-Lussac's) observed experimentally B) Only chemical reactions, not physical gas behavior C) The color of gases only D) Nuclear structure of atoms

134. Diffusion of gases, explained by kinetic theory, occurs because: A) Gas molecules are in constant random motion, spreading spontaneously from high to low concentration regions B) Gas molecules are stationary and diffusion is a chemical process C) Gas molecules repel each other so strongly they cannot mix D) Diffusion only occurs in liquids, not gases

135. An extraordinary/everyday demonstration of kinetic theory is Brownian motion, which shows: A) Random, erratic movement of microscopic particles (e.g., pollen in water) due to continuous collisions with fast-moving invisible molecules B) The complete absence of molecular motion in fluids C) That molecules move in perfectly straight, unchanging paths forever D) That gas molecules are visible to the naked eye

136. According to kinetic theory, absolute zero (0 K) represents the temperature at which: A) The translational kinetic energy of gas molecules would theoretically become zero B) Gas molecules move fastest C) Gas pressure becomes infinite D) Gas molecules become chemically inert
